question: Who was elected President of Pakistan in March 2024?
detailedExplanation: Asif Ali Zardari was elected as the 14th President of Pakistan on 9 March 2024 and took oath on 10 March 2024. He previously served as President from 2008 to 2013. He is the co-chairman of the Pakistan Peoples Party.
subject: current-affairs

question: Who took oath as the 24th Prime Minister of Pakistan in March 2024?
detailedExplanation: Shehbaz Sharif took oath as Prime Minister of Pakistan on 4 March 2024 after the general elections of 8 February 2024. He had earlier served as PM from April 2022 to August 2023. This was his second term.
subject: current-affairs

question: The general elections in Pakistan were held on which date in February 2024?
detailedExplanation: Pakistan's general elections were held on 8 February 2024 for the National Assembly and provincial assemblies. The PTI-backed independent candidates won the largest number of National Assembly seats.
subject: current-affairs

question: The 26th Constitutional Amendment of Pakistan was passed by Parliament in which month and year?
detailedExplanation: The 26th Constitutional Amendment was passed by both houses of Parliament in October 2024. It created constitutional benches in the Supreme Court, revised the Chief Justice appointment process, and reduced National Assembly seats to 336.
subject: current-affairs

question: In September 2024, the IMF approved a new extended fund facility (EFF) for Pakistan of about:
detailedExplanation: The IMF Executive Board approved a 37-month Extended Fund Facility of about US$7 billion for Pakistan in September 2024, under a programme aimed at macroeconomic stabilization and structural reforms.
subject: current-affairs

question: Which Pakistani cricketer was the leading run scorer for Pakistan in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, held in Pakistan and the UAE?
detailedExplanation: Babar Azam was Pakistan's leading run-scorer in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025. The tournament was hosted by Pakistan (with UAE co-hosting for India's matches), and India won the title by beating New Zealand in the final.
subject: current-affairs

question: Pakistan hosted which major ICC tournament in 2025, the first global ICC event on its soil in nearly three decades?
detailedExplanation: Pakistan hosted the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 (February-March 2025) - the first major ICC event in Pakistan since the 1996 World Cup. Matches were held in Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi, with India's matches moved to Dubai under the hybrid model.
subject: current-affairs

question: Who is the Chief of the Army Staff of Pakistan as of mid-2026?
optionC: General Syed Asim Munir Ahmed Shah
detailedExplanation: General Syed Asim Munir Ahmed Shah assumed charge as the 17th Chief of Army Staff on 29 November 2022, succeeding General Qamar Javed Bajwa. He is a former Director General of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI).
subject: current-affairs

question: The current Chief Justice of Azad Jammu and Kashmir's Supreme Court is:
detailedExplanation: Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan is the current Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Azad Jammu and Kashmir, appointed in 2025. The AJK Supreme Court is the highest court of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir region.
subject: current-affairs

question: Pakistan's primary stated reason for airstrikes on Afghanistan in February-March 2026 was:
optionA: Capturing TTP leaders hiding in Kabul
optionB: Targeting militant camps linked to TTP and ISIS-K that attack Pakistan
optionD: Securing water rights from the Kabul River
detailedExplanation: Pakistan conducted airstrikes in Afghanistan in February-March 2026 targeting camps of Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and ISIS-K linked militants used for cross-border attacks on Pakistan. The strikes raised tensions with Afghanistan's interim government.
subject: current-affairs

question: In March 2026, Meta and YouTube were found liable by a US court in a landmark case related to:
detailedExplanation: A landmark US court case in March 2026 held Meta and YouTube liable for contributing to social media addiction among young users. The ruling is seen as a precedent for tech platforms' duty of care over addictive features.
subject: current-affairs

question: India hosted which G20 summit in 2023, under its presidency?
detailedExplanation: India hosted the 18th G20 Summit in New Delhi on 9-10 September 2023 under its G20 presidency. The New Delhi Leaders' Declaration was adopted, which included a historic consensus on the African Union's membership in the G20.
subject: current-affairs

question: The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of which global grouping in September 2023?
detailedExplanation: At the New Delhi G20 Summit (9-10 September 2023), the African Union was formally admitted as a permanent member of the G20, making it the second regional bloc (after the EU) to hold full membership.
subject: current-affairs

question: Which countries joined BRICS as new members in 2024?
detailedExplanation: Iran, the UAE, Ethiopia and Egypt joined BRICS as new members in January 2024, following the Johannesburg Summit of 2023. Saudi Arabia was invited but did not formally join at that time.
subject: current-affairs

question: Who is the Secretary-General of the United Nations?
detailedExplanation: Antonio Guterres of Portugal has been the UN Secretary-General since 1 January 2017. His current term runs to 31 December 2026. Ban Ki-moon (2007-2016) and Kofi Annan (1997-2006) were his predecessors.
subject: current-affairs

question: The 2024 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP29) was hosted by which country?
detailedExplanation: COP29 was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024. A landmark outcome was the agreement on a New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) of at least US$300 billion per year in climate finance for developing countries by 2035.
subject: current-affairs

question: The COP30 climate summit of 2025 was held in which city?
detailedExplanation: COP30 took place in Belém, Brazil, in November 2025 - the first COP held in the Amazon region. It focused on accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels and finalizing rules on carbon markets under the Paris Agreement.
subject: current-affairs

question: In 2024, NASA's Artemis programme launched which mission carrying a crew around the Moon?
detailedExplanation: Artemis II, launched in November 2024, carried a four-person crew around the Moon and back - the first crewed lunar flyby since Apollo 17 in 1972. Artemis III is planned as the first crewed lunar landing of the programme.
subject: current-affairs

question: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed near which region of the Moon in August 2023?
detailedExplanation: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar South Pole on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to land a spacecraft in that region and the fourth to achieve a soft landing on the Moon, after the USSR, USA and China.
subject: current-affairs

question: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in which city?
detailedExplanation: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France (26 July - 11 August 2024). The United States topped the medal table, and the Games featured debut sports including breakdancing. Los Angeles will host the 2028 Games.
subject: current-affairs

question: Pakistan's quota-holding Olympic weightlifter who qualified for Paris 2024 was:
detailedExplanation: Haider Fayaz became the first Pakistani weightlifter in 40 years to qualify for the Olympics when he earned a quota for the Paris 2024 Games. Pakistan's last Olympic gold came in 1984 (hockey). In Paris, Arshad Nadeem won gold in javelin.
subject: current-affairs

question: Arshad Nadeem won Pakistan's first individual Olympic gold medal in 2024 in which event?
detailedExplanation: Arshad Nadeem won gold in the javelin throw at the Paris 2024 Olympics with an Olympic record of 92.97 metres - Pakistan's first individual Olympic gold and its first Olympic gold since the 1984 hockey team.
subject: current-affairs

question: The 2024 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to:
detailedExplanation: The 2024 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Nihon Hidankyo, the Japanese organization of atomic bomb survivors from Hiroshima and Nagasaki, for their efforts to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons.
subject: current-affairs

question: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has its headquarters in:
detailedExplanation: The OIC, founded in 1969 after the Rabat summit, has its headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. It is the second largest intergovernmental organization after the UN, with 57 member states. Pakistan is a founding member.
subject: current-affairs

question: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) was founded in which year?
detailedExplanation: The SCO was founded on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Pakistan and India became full members in 2017. Its secretariat is in Beijing.
subject: current-affairs

question: The SAARC Charter was signed in 1985 in which city?
detailedExplanation: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was founded on 8 December 1985 when its charter was adopted in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Its secretariat is located in Kathmandu, Nepal.
subject: current-affairs

question: The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted in which year?
detailedExplanation: The Paris Agreement was adopted on 12 December 2015 at COP21 in Paris and entered into force on 4 November 2016. Its goal is to limit global warming to well below 2C, pursuing efforts to keep it to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels.
subject: current-affairs

question: Which treaty is considered the legal basis for Pakistan's and India's nuclear-related relations after 1998?
detailedExplanation: The Lahore Declaration, signed by PMs Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee in February 1999, committed Pakistan and India to dialogue, confidence building and nuclear risk reduction. The NPT is a global treaty, and Pakistan is not a signatory.
subject: current-affairs

question: The Commonwealth of Nations, of which Pakistan is a member, is headquartered in:
detailedExplanation: The Commonwealth Secretariat is headquartered in London. Pakistan joined the Commonwealth in 1947, left it in 1972 (after Bangladesh's recognition), rejoined in 1989, was suspended in 1999 and 2007, and was re-admitted in 2008.
subject: current-affairs

question: Which Pakistani was re-elected as a judge of the International Court of Justice in 2024?
detailedExplanation: Justice Muhammad Imran Ali Qazi of Pakistan was re-elected to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in 2024 for a second nine-year term (2024-2033). He had first been elected in 2015.
subject: current-affairs
